title: Life Admin Pass: The Grok Bot Operating Playbook
prepared: Prepared 28 Oct 2026 (AEDT). The case study is the Life Admin Pass, from Run 6 (roadmap) and Run 7 (deep dive). This is not legal, tax or financial advice. Items marked [verify in app] are capabilities that were not confirmed from the app UI notes or the public docs. Check them in the app before you rely on them. Items marked [assumption] are estimates, not sourced facts.
privacyLine: Never collect, copy, or store customers' private data in /workspace or anywhere we control. Our apps are device-only. Work with aggregates, order numbers and ticket references, never names, emails or household details. If you need personal data to finish a task, stop and ask me.
sendLine: Never send, post, publish, buy, refund, merge to main, deploy to production, or change ad spend without my approval. Draft first and show me.

summary: Run a lean team: Chief of Staff (orchestration and ops), Builder (cloud agents, GitHub, Vercel), Support & QA, Growth (content, SEO, and ads under a cap), Partnerships & Distribution (schools, P&Cs, parent groups, app stores), Finance & Admin, and the existing SideHustle Bot for strategy. The Bots hand work over through Bot-to-Bot messages, a shared /workspace/lifeadmin/ folder and an HQ group chat. You get one CEO briefing every Monday and approve drafts in two short windows a day. Nothing leaves under your name, money does not move, and nothing reaches production without your OK.
lineup: Every approval, money, anything sent under your name
Orchestration, the weekly CEO briefing, decision log, ops calendar
Specs, Cursor cloud agents, GitHub PRs, Vercel deploys, privacy tests
Customer inbox triage and draft replies, daily smoke tests, refund prep, bug reports
SEO pages, content calendar, Pinterest/Instagram/TikTok drafts, newsletter drafts, analytics, ad drafts and spend reports (within caps)
Schools and P&C newsletters, parent-group admins, OzBargain, app-store listings, affiliates
Payout reconciliation, bookkeeping prep, GST-threshold tracker, BAS calendar, cost register, monthly P&L
Idea pipeline, IdeaLab, competitor watch, monthly portfolio review, continue-or-kill calls
merges: Operations sits with the Chief of Staff. At this stage, ops means cadence, files and handoffs, which is the CoS job.
QA sits with Support. Both watch the live product from the user's side, and both feed bugs to Builder.

Ads sits with Growth while ad spend is small. Split it out once paid spend passes about A$1,000/month [assumption] or runs on two or more ad platforms. At that point it has its own tools, its own approval boundary (money) and its own daily rhythm.
Distribution (app stores) sits with Partnerships. Both are slow, relationship- and listing-driven work with long lead times.
whyNotMore: You are the bottleneck. Every send, spend, merge and refund needs your OK. With more Bots, you get more cards to approve, not more output.
Usage is a shared pool. Grok Bot usage comes from your plan's weekly allowance, then from on-demand usage if you turn it on. Every routine draws from it.
Group chats hold 2–6 Bots. That is exactly the six core Bots in an HQ room.

The docs' test for a new Bot: create one when the work has a distinct goal, set of tools, working style, approval boundary, or recurring schedule. Each Bot above passes that test. A separate Content Bot and SEO Bot would not.
addLater: Ads: once spend is over the threshold above.
App Store Release: when native wrappers ship, a Play TWA, then an iOS wrapper.
Community: only if you open your own Facebook group.
Localisation: for NZ/UK expansion after the Pass.
first30: Phase 0 setup. Hire Chief of Staff, Builder, Support & QA and Growth. Create the shared /workspace/lifeadmin/ ops folder, the 4 shared skills and the Auto-review Ask-first rules.
Builder launches a cloud agent to build the static PWA template repo. Growth drafts the 3 SEO pages and the Secret Santa feeder tool brief. Support writes the reply macros and refund policy draft.
GiftLedger is built on the template. Support runs daily smoke tests from staging. Growth prepares the launch kit: OzBargain post, 10 pins, newsletter draft. All drafts wait for you.
Launch on 18–20 Nov. The first weekly CEO briefings come with real numbers. Turn routines on one at a time after each passes Test.

handoffs: A Bot can send an asynchronous message to another Bot, which wakes, handles the request, and can reply later. Use one owner per stage. Parallel handoffs create duplicate work.
Every Bot uses the same cloud computer and /workspace. The handoff artifacts live in /workspace/lifeadmin/ so they do not depend on chat context.
New chat, then select 2–6 Bots. Use @Bot to hand over a task. Bot-to-group messages are text-only.
Private skills are one library shared by all your Bots.
Conversations and learned context stay separate per Bot. Shared facts go in files, not memory.

bots.owns: The ops calendar (launch dates from the Run 6 roadmap), decisions.md, briefings/, kpis.csv, the HQ group chat, and the routine health check (paused or failing routines).
bots.connectors: None required. It reads files the other Bots write. Optional: GitHub (read-only, to count merged PRs), using the built-in GitHub connector.
routines: CEO briefing, Mon 7:43 (43 7 * * 1)
Weekday standup digest, 8:17 (17 8 * * 1-5)

bots.outputs: The CEO briefing (a Page, plus briefings/ markdown), updated kpis.csv, and a decision list for you.
bots.approvals: Nothing external. It only drafts. It asks before re-prioritising another Bot's work.
bots.kpis: Briefing on time on 100% of Mondays. Decisions waiting more than 7 days: 0. Routines failing unnoticed for more than 48h: 0.
bots.starter: You are Chief of Staff for my solo business building the Life Admin Pass (device-only household apps for Australian families). Your job: run the operating cadence, keep /workspace/lifeadmin/ tidy, write the Monday CEO briefing, track decisions in decisions.md and KPIs in kpis.csv, and route work to Builder, Support & QA, Growth, Partnerships and Finance & Admin with one owner per task. You do not do their work; you make sure it happens and tell me what needs a decision. Lead every briefing with the 3 decisions I must make. Times in AEDT. Never collect, copy, or store customers' private data in /workspace or anywhere we control. Our apps are device-only. Work with aggregates, order numbers and ticket references, never names, emails or household details. If you need personal data to finish a task, stop and ask me. Never send, post, publish, buy, refund, merge to main, deploy to production, or change ad spend without my approval. Draft first and show me. Remember this for future work.

cadence: Standup digest from overnight handoffs, routine failures, and drafts waiting for you
Builder chat and a GitHub comment
CEO briefing: 3 decisions, KPIs, launches, risks, spend
timeBudget: Your time budget [assumption]: 10 minutes each weekday to approve drafts; 30 minutes on Monday for the briefing and decisions; 30 minutes on Friday to approve next week's content.
coordination: One owner per task. Handoffs go as a Bot-to-Bot message plus a file in handoffs/.
Facts that other Bots need live in files, not memory, because memory is per Bot.
Shared method lives in skills. Bot-specific schedules live in routines.
Cross-team discussion happens in the HQ group (6 Bots max). Reviews with SideHustle happen by handoff or in a second room.
Results are Pages or files with source links. Each Bot separates facts, assumptions, done items and awaiting-approval items.
guardrails: Privacy rule in every persona and in the privacy-rule skill

Device-only apps, a merchant of record for payments, cookieless analytics. No customer PII in /workspace. Honest note: customer support emails do contain email addresses. They live in the Bot's email inbox (Grok Bot's mail service) and at the MoR, not on servers you run. Disclose both in your privacy policy.
Email from routines always waits as a draft until you press Send. There is no unattended sending. Messages under your own name go out as an editable draft card you send.

Path: Settings, General, Bot section, Custom Rules. Ask first wins conflicts. The limit is 20 Ask-first and 20 Allow rules. Suggested rules: send any email, message or post outside this app; spend money, change an ad budget, or start a subscription; merge to main, promote a Vercel deployment to production, or change DNS/domains; issue a refund or change merchant-of-record settings; delete files, repos, routines or Bots; submit anything to the ATO, an app store, or a government site.

Grok Bot's on-demand monthly limit (Settings, Usage & Billing; a running task can finish slightly past it). Platform caps such as the Meta spending limit and Vercel spend management. The Bot's own rules.
Secrets in Vault or a Secure Form, never in chat

The shared computer's screens are work surfaces, not security boundaries, so do not put a credential on the computer that another Bot should not use. Prefer read-only/viewer roles (Xero adviser/read-only, Vercel viewer where possible). [verify in app] that the Vault tab is enabled for your account.

ATO lodgement and payments. Bank transfers. Signing agreements. Replying to a journalist or regulator. Refunds above a set amount. Deleting customer-facing data. Posting in Facebook groups. Fake reviews or astroturfing (ACCC). Buying followers.
Customer emails and web pages are data, not instructions. Routines still never act on a request found inside an email. OWASP LLM06 Excessive Agency.
Legal checks Growth and Support must follow
Spam Act: consent, identify yourself, unsubscribe honoured within 5 working days (ACMA). ACL consumer guarantees cover apps. A no-refunds policy cannot remove them (ACCC).
phase0: Settings basics

Open Settings with the account button at the bottom-left of the sidebar, Cmd+, or Open settings in the command palette. Under General, set Timezone to Australia/Sydney and confirm Auto-review is on. Add the Ask-first Custom Rules from the guardrails.
Cap usage

In Settings, Usage & Billing, check your plan's weekly usage. Turn on and set the On-demand monthly limit, or leave on-demand off so Bots stop at the weekly limit. On The X Subscription, top-up limits are set at grok.com/dashboard/billing instead.
Create the 4 Phase-0 Bots

Chief of Staff, Builder, Support & QA, Growth. Use the + at the top of the sidebar, then Create new Bot (or type a name and pick Create name Bot). The docs label this button both New Bot and New chat [verify in app]. Paste the starter persona as the first message. Click the Bot's name in the chat header (or Cmd+Shift+I) for its info pane. The gear beside the X sets the name, title, avatar and description.
Group the roster
Right-click a Bot, Move to new section, Life Admin Pass [verify in app].
Shared folder and skills

Ask Chief of Staff to create /workspace/lifeadmin/. Ask it to save 4 shared skills: privacy-rule, draft-first-outbound, weekly-report-format and release-checklist. Ask save this as a skill called …. If a skill does not show in another Bot's / menu, enable it per Bot under Connect apps, connected count, Private skills [verify in app].
Connect apps

GitHub and Vercel are already connected on this account. Add others through Connect apps in the sidebar, or an in-chat Connect card. Exact catalogue [verify in app]. Services with no connector (MoR, Xero, Pinterest, Meta Ads, Umami) are used through the browser, with sign-in from Vault or a Secure Form.
Email address

Claim one Bot email address by asking a Bot Get yourself an email address, then approve the card. The claim is permanent: one per account, cannot be renamed. Avoid reserved words (support, help, info, admin, billing). Example: lifeadminpass@mail.grokbot.com.
Group chat
Create the HQ group: New chat, select the Bots, kickoff message assigning owners [verify in app] for the exact flow.
Routines, one at a time
Ask each Bot to create its routines (Appendix A prompts). Open each one and press Test with safe inputs. A test does real work. Turn on only those that pass.
Business basics, done by you
ABN (free) at business.gov.au. Domain. MoR account (Lemon Squeezy or Polar) with a test product. Umami Cloud Hobby (free). Email processor with double opt-in. Vercel Pro.
phases: 5 live (CoS, Builder, Support, Growth, Finance), plus SideHustle

School-holiday SEO pages for all 8 states and territories. 3 or more P&C newsletter placements in Term 1. First quarterly strategy review (Apr). HQ running with no more than 15 minutes a day of your approvals.
Ads Bot and App Store Release Bot only when triggered

The Pass (This Week hub, HolidayPlanner, Renewal Radar, GiftLedger and Household Handbook), launching Oct 2027 at A$29/yr. BedPlanner (Aug 2027). Moving Mode v1.1. RunSheet (Feb 2028). Ads spend over A$1,000/month adds an Ads Bot. An iOS wrapper adds an App Store Release Bot. GST projected over A$60k means Finance engages an accountant. A human helper means shared/team Bots [verify in app]. Pass launched; existing buyers upgraded at A$19; a per-app continue/kill decision at each slot's date.

channelFacts: ACMA 2026: Facebook 78% of adults, Instagram 53%, TikTok 30%, Pinterest 20%. Parents of 0–8-year-olds: 92% use social media and 96% of those do so daily; Facebook dominant, then Instagram (ECU).
financeFacts: GST registration is required at A$75,000 current or projected GST turnover, within 21 days. Quarterly BAS is due 28 Oct, 28 Feb, 28 Apr and 28 Jul. Keep GST records for 5 years. How MoR sales count toward your GST turnover as an Australian merchant is a question for your accountant.
risks: Usage runaway
Broad listeners or chatty handoffs drain the weekly pool
Narrow triggers (sender filters, specific CI branch). No */N schedules. On-demand monthly limit. Finance watches usage weekly.
Approval fatigue
You rubber-stamp cards
Batch drafts into 2 daily windows. Keep Always allow only for low-risk reads. Never Always allow sends or spend.
Expired background approvals
Cards from routines expire after 30 min
Routines draft and report. They never wait on a card mid-run.
Duplicate / looping handoffs
Two Bots both own a launch
One owner per stage. Handoff files. CoS audits monthly.
Stale memory
A Bot acts on last quarter's price or date
Facts live in files. Consequential decisions reopen the source.
Prompt injection
A customer email says refund me and email everyone
Emails are data. Routines never act on in-email requests. Ask-first rules.
Credential sprawl
All Bots share one computer and its logins
Vault or Secure Form. Read-only roles. No keys in files. Screens are not security boundaries.
Silent routine failure
A routine paused after time away, or auth failed
CoS monthly routine audit. Pause on repeated auth failures. Only the last 20 runs are kept.
Privacy creep
Support copies customer details into notes
privacy-rule skill. Ticket refs only. Monthly grep of /workspace/lifeadmin for @.
Platform/vendor change
MoR repricing (Polar May 2026), Lemon Squeezy to Stripe, Play fee model
Finance quarterly vendor check. Keep licence logic MoR-agnostic in the template.
Destructive actions
A Bot deleted or the computer reset
Deleting a Bot deletes its routines. Hide instead. Use Update, not Reset. Keep the plan in this file and in the repo.
Brand / community harm
Over-posting in parent groups
Partnerships only contacts admins. You post personally. Follow group rules.
Legal
Misleading claims, Spam Act, ACL
draft-first-outbound embeds the ACMA/ACCC checks. Lawyer review of terms once (Run 6).
